title: Oliver's playing and the band breaking up
summary: He describes Oliver's weakened lip and the band splitting up in New York, then a six-week job afterwards.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: But we left New Orleans, a little red alley. And the fellow named Paul. Paul Barnes.
Paul Barnes, yes. He's in California. He was back home though for about two months in the fall. He played there.

We left New Orleans together to go to St. Burst and George to kill Oliver. You know. So King Oliver Band split up on the county. He turned down a regular job, you know. Not as a larger salary. But the fellow said he'd be walking around New York in the streets. Yeah. Then another fellow had a...
Excuse me. How did Oliver play in those days? Was his lip still good? Was he powerful when you joined him in St. Louis?

Not as much as it was before. He was good in his lip. He had that power and he couldn't, didn't have much pressure. Did he play every piece or just now and then play a little bit? Between, just between. He had good cornets there to help him. Yeah, he had went down on that.
